research_sources.title: Hardware-Efficient FPGA Implementation of Sigmoid Function Using Mixed-Radix Hyperbolic Rotation CORDIC
research_sources.status: arXiv author manuscript; reports acceptance at 2AI 2026
research_sources.comparison_role: Closest recent pipelined CORDIC sigmoid comparator
research_sources.notes: Dedicated hardware per iteration. Restricted sigmoid input domain [-1;1]. Reports MAE 4.23e-4 and zero DSP. Resource figure 835 is inconsistently described as LUTs and slices; do not treat those units as interchangeable. Requires matched-domain and same-device resynthesis for a fair numerical comparison.

research_sources.title: A Systolic Array Architecture for Nonlinear Activation Functions and Softmax Computation using Chebyshev Polynomials
research_sources.status: arXiv author manuscript; reports acceptance at IEEE COINS 2026
research_sources.notes: Uses a 10-row polynomial array with 8 or 16 columns. Evaluates tanh and sigmoid across [-4;4]; supports softmax too. Useful algorithm and accuracy comparator. ASIC area and power cannot be compared directly with PYNQ FPGA LUTs or power.

research_sources.title: CORDIC Is All You Need
research_sources.notes: Combines CORDIC MAC and nonlinear functions in a reconfigurable systolic architecture. Workload and pruning differ from this four-output NPU. Do not transfer its reported system speedups to this design; separate MAC and activation results when discussing it.

research_sources.title: An Area-Efficient and Low-Error FPGA-Based Sigmoid Function Approximation
research_sources.technology: Multiple FPGA families; 16-bit with 12 fractional bits
research_sources.notes: Publishes VHDL and Octave source. Piecewise first/second-degree polynomial sigmoid; reported MAE 1.66e-3 over [-8;8]. Strong methodological baseline because implementations use consistent precision and targets. Our 14-fractional-bit results need requantization before a direct comparison.

research_sources.title: EBACA: Efficient Bfloat16-based Activation Function Implementation Using Enhanced CORDIC Architecture
research_sources.notes: Presents serial/parallel/hybrid softmax architectures and tanh/sigmoid hardware. Useful evidence for area-throughput tradeoffs; BF16 and this project's fixed point have different accuracy and range, so they are not directly equivalent.
